titleText.es: Oye, ¿qué probabilidad había de que hubiera cinco fans de Ayn Rand en el mismo tren? Deben de ir a una convención.
titleText.en: Hey, what are the odds -- five Ayn Rand fans on the same train! Must be going to a convention.
titleText.noteEn: The official English title blends sheep and people as Sheeple. The Spanish archive uses the broader livestock title Ganado while preserving the sheep comparison in ovejas.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: An autómata is a machine or a person imagined as moving without independent thought. The plural autómatas can refer to a mixed or masculine group.

example.es: La novela presenta a los trabajadores como autómatas.
example.en: The novel presents the workers as automatons.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Bovina describes a feminine singular noun and can literally mean related to cattle or figuratively suggest a dull, passive expression.

example.es: La figura tenía una expresión bovina.
example.en: The figure had a bovine expression.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Sometidos comes from someter. Its -os ending matches a masculine or mixed plural group.

example.es: Los planes están sometidos a revisión.
example.en: The plans are subject to review.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to; required after sometido before what imposes the constraint
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Sometido, sometida, sometidos, and sometidas normally use a before the rule, force, or condition that something is subject to.

example.es: El horario está sometido a cambios.
example.en: The schedule is subject to changes.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Diaria is the feminine singular form of diario because it describes a feminine singular noun.

example.es: Caminar forma parte de mi rutina diaria.
example.en: Walking is part of my daily routine.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Pararse uses the attached pronoun se. Before another action, pararse a means to stop what one is doing in order to perform that action.

example.es: Se paró a escuchar la música.
example.en: He stopped to listen to the music.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: ever (after a negative idea such as sin)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Nunca often means ‘never.’ When sin has already supplied the negative meaning, natural English commonly uses ‘ever’: sin mirar nunca atrás means ‘without ever looking back.’

example.en: He left without ever looking back.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to; links pararse to the action someone stops to do
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Use a between a form of pararse and the following action verb in its unchanged dictionary form.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; begins a su alrededor, ‘around them’
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The location expression uses a before mi, tu, or su alrededor. Natural English translates the whole expression rather than a by itself.
In a mi, tu, or su alrededor, alrededor refers to the surrounding area and natural English says ‘around me, you, him, her, or them.’
Único changes to única, únicos, or únicas to match the person or thing it describes.

example.en: It is the only open road.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Consciente has the same singular form for masculine and feminine nouns; its plural is conscientes.

example.en: I am aware of the problem.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Oveja is grammatically feminine. The plural ovejas can refer to multiple sheep regardless of their sex.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone or something is subject to a rule, force, or condition?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use the matching form of sometido followed by a and the condition.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Choose sometido, sometida, sometidos, or sometidas to match the person or thing affected. The preposition a remains unchanged before what imposes the control or constraint.

example.es: La decisión está sometida a varias reglas.
example.en: The decision is subject to several rules.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone pauses in order to do an action?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use the needed form of pararse, then a, then the action verb in its unchanged dictionary form.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The small pronoun changes with the person: me paro, te paras, se para, nos paramos, or se paran. A remains before the following action.

example.es: Nos paramos a leer el aviso.
example.en: We stopped to read the notice.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say ‘around me,’ ‘around you,’ ‘around us,’ or a similar idea?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a, then a possessive word such as mi, tu, su, nuestro, or vuestro, then alrededor.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The possessive word identifies whose surrounding area is meant. Su can refer to one or more people, so the situation tells whether it means around him, her, or them; nuestro means around us, and vuestro means around plural informal ‘you’ in Spain.

example.es: Miramos a nuestro alrededor antes de seguir.
example.en: We looked around us before continuing.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: autómatas · único ser humano consciente · mundo de ovejas
cardDefinitions.questionEn: What undercuts the speaker's claim to be the only independent thinker?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: The same thought bubble belongs to all five train passengers: each person privately believes everyone else is an unthinking sheep while imagining themself uniquely conscious. Their supposedly individual insight is therefore identical and collective.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The official English title Sheeple blends sheep and people. The title text calls the passengers Ayn Rand fans; Rand is associated with philosophical individualism, which sharpens the irony of five people making the same self-exception.

applications.explanationEn: Mira is the affirmative informal command used to tell one familiar person to look.
Sometidos comes after the expanded noun phrase headed by autómatas and describes that group.
Sometidos uses masculine plural -os to match the mixed or masculine plural group autómatas.
Bovina follows the noun mirada in the common neutral order for a descriptive adjective.
Bovina uses feminine singular -a to match the feminine singular noun mirada.
Sometidos matches the plural people, a introduces the controlling condition, and su rutina diaria fills that condition slot.
Diaria follows rutina in the common neutral order for a descriptive adjective.
Diaria uses feminine singular -a to match the feminine singular noun rutina.
Sin introduces an action that does not happen, and pararse remains in its unchanged dictionary form with se attached.
The pronoun se is attached to the end of the unchanged infinitive parar, producing the single written word pararse.
Pararse supplies the pause, a links it to the next action, and mirar stays in its unchanged dictionary form; nunca adds the visible ‘ever’ meaning inside the negative setting.
A and alrededor form the location expression, while su identifies the people whose surroundings are meant.
Humano follows the noun ser, and consciente follows that complete noun expression to add a second description of the same being.
Único and humano use masculine singular -o to match ser. Consciente is also singular; its ending works with either masculine or feminine nouns, while its plural would be conscientes.

applications.exampleEs: SOY EL ÚNICO SER HUMANO CONSCIENTE
applications.explanationEn: Soy is a form of ser because the following noun phrase presents the speaker's claimed identity rather than a physical location.
